name: ledit
why: An old OCaml line editor wrapper that adds readline-style editing to any interactive command; a small piece of history with a mild huh.

brief.what_it_is: Ledit is a line editor that lets interactive shell commands use Emacs-style control characters for editing input. The homepage describes it as allowing shell commands to be used with control characters like in emacs. The README adds that it works with interactive commands and gives bash and tcsh as the shells whose control-command style it follows. It is written in OCaml and uses the unix library. The README does not describe the input and output in detail beyond that.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a way to get shell-style control-command editing (as in emacs, bash, or tcsh) for interactive commands. The homepage says it allows shell commands to be used with control characters like in emacs.
brief.install_notes: You need OCaml and Camlp5 to compile it. The README says both are free and downloadable on the Web. The homepage has a Distribution section with a download link for the sources and a link to a directory of all versions. Neither the homepage nor the README gives an install command or any configuration or first-run steps. The brew description has no caveats.
brief.standout: It is a small, old OCaml tool that wraps an existing interactive command to add readline-style editing, rather than being built into a shell. Its README is only a few lines and the project is a self-contained historical artifact from Inria.
brief.status: quiet. The homepage says the current distributed version is 2.04, released 2018-01-24. The README copyright runs 2001-2012. I found no newer release or commit information, and the homepage does not say whether the project is still maintained.
brief.caveats: It must be compiled from source with OCaml and Camlp5, so there is no ready-made binary path in what I read. The README's copyright notice is Inria's, and the license is only linked as a LICENSE file on the homepage, which I did not fetch, so I cannot state the license terms. Development appears to have stopped years ago. The homepage link to CHANGES and the LICENSE file were not followed.
quotes: Ledit is a line editor, allowing to use control commands like in emacs or in shells (bash, tcsh).
To be used with interactive commands. It is written in OCaml and uses the library unix.cma.
